record.title: Kumu Hina
record.year_scope: Original documentary and festival premiere year stated by the film project. PBS debut was in May 2015; the selected complete YouTube edition was uploaded October 20, 2024.
record.credits: Directed and produced by Dean Hamer and Joe Wilson; co-producer Connie M. Florez. The film site credits Hinaleimoana Wong-Kalu as Haku Moʻolelo and narrator.
record.publisher: Qwaves / Lei Pua ʻAla Queer Histories of Hawaiʻi
record.synopsis: Native Hawaiian teacher Hina Wong-Kalu supports a student’s leadership in a Honolulu hula troupe while navigating her own marriage. The documentary explores māhū identity, cultural learning and belonging.
record.perspective: Centers Hina Wong-Kalu and school participants, with Hina credited as Haku Moʻolelo and narrator in a Qwaves production. These situated stories do not represent every Native Hawaiian or māhū person.
record.availability: The film project links this complete edition free on the Lei Pua ʻAla YouTube channel. Only English auto-generated captions are listed. Regional or account limits may apply; actual playback and caption quality are unverified.
record.content_note: Explores gender identity, mixed reactions to a student’s leadership and conflict within a marriage.
